name: Harbor
what_it_is: A framework for evaluating agents: each task is a folder (instruction, container image, verifier), and Harbor runs any agent on it in a sandbox (Docker, Modal, Daytona and others), records a reward and a trajectory, and can generate rollouts for RL.
use_it_when: You want one portable task format and a single command that runs any agent on many sandboxed tasks in parallel and writes a score for each attempt.
source_note: GitHub README (features list, install, Terminal-Bench example) and the repo's homepage field.

name: Hatchery
what_it_is: A shared workspace for RL environments: versioned task revisions, review comments on exact task lines, automated per-dataset checks, agent runs from a CLI, and benchmark pages built from labelled jobs; it states it is fully compatible with Harbor.
use_it_when: A team is writing and reviewing many Harbor-style tasks and wants checks (oracle passes, instruction complete, no private data) and reviews tied to each task revision.
source_note: hatchery.build landing page (feature list, `hatchery run --path . --remote --agent oracle`, Harbor compatibility line). The page does not say whether it is open source or what it costs.

name: Halo
what_it_is: An open-source training framework for language and multimodal models (pre-training, SFT, preference optimisation, fully asynchronous multi-turn RL) whose environmental GRPO runs custom Python environments against a separate vLLM or SGLang rollout server.
use_it_when: You have a multi-turn environment and several GPUs, and want asynchronous GRPO with reward terms (tests, LLM judges, checklists) on a Hugging Face model; its environment trainer needs the rollout server on different GPUs from the trainer.
source_note: README on origin/main (9f32a5f7), LICENSE, agent-docs/training-methods/async-grpo/setup.md (GPU split) and environments/custom.md (EnvironmentBase with _reset_single, _step_single, _grade_episode).

name: verifiers + Environments Hub
what_it_is: A library for defining tasksets, running agents and harnesses on them, and scoring them for evaluation and RL, tied to a public hub of installable user-made environments and to the prime-rl trainer; it can also load Harbor tasks.
use_it_when: You want to publish an environment others can install and run with one command, or train on someone else's environment with prime-rl.
source_note: GitHub README, docs/overview.md (taskset, harness, agent, environment, trace) and docs/harbor.md (HarborTaskset for single-step Harbor tasks).

name: OpenEnv
what_it_is: A framework for building and deploying isolated execution environments for agentic RL with a Gymnasium-style reset()/step()/state() API over a WebSocket; each environment is a Docker image that can run locally, in a cloud sandbox or as a Hugging Face Space, with 40+ ready environments.
use_it_when: You want your environment to run as a separate server that several trainers (TRL, Unsloth, SkyRL, ART and others) can talk to, or want a ready game, coding or browser environment.
source_note: GitHub README ('What you get' list, quick start). The repo now lives under the openenv organisation.

name: Gymnasium
what_it_is: The standard Python API between RL algorithms and environments (the maintained fork of OpenAI Gym), with reference environments such as Classic Control, Box2D, Toy Text, MuJoCo and Atari.
use_it_when: You are learning the reset/step contract itself, or your environment is a classic control or game problem rather than a language-model chat.

name: TRL (GRPOTrainer environments)
what_it_is: Hugging Face's post-training library; its GRPOTrainer trains agents with stateless `tools` or a stateful `environment_factory` (a class with reset(), public methods exposed as tools, and an optional get_reward), with OpenEnv, Harbor (trl.experimental.harbor) and OpenReward integrations.
use_it_when: You already use Hugging Face models and want GRPO over a small Python environment on one machine with the least new infrastructure.
source_note: docs/source/grpo_trainer.md ('Agent Training': tools vs environment_factory), docs/source/openenv.md and docs/source/harbor.md on main.

name: verl
what_it_is: A production RL post-training library (the open version of the HybridFlow paper) that builds GRPO or PPO dataflows on top of FSDP, Megatron-LM, vLLM and SGLang, with flexible placement of models on GPUs.
use_it_when: You need throughput at scale on many GPUs and are fine with a heavier, configuration-driven stack; other tools (rLLM, SkyRL recipes) use it as a backend.
source_note: GitHub README (overview and news). The repo moved from volcengine/verl to the verl-project organisation.

name: SkyRL
what_it_is: A modular full-stack RL library for LLMs: a trainer (skyrl, which also implements the Tinker API), an agent layer for long-horizon multi-turn tool use (skyrl-agent), and skyrl-gym, a set of math, coding, search and SQL environments in the Gymnasium API; it integrates with Harbor.
use_it_when: You want a research-friendly trainer for multi-turn tool-use agents, with ready Gymnasium-style text environments to start from.
source_note: GitHub README (overview of skyrl, skyrl-agent, skyrl-gym; news item on the Harbor integration). The repo moved from NovaSky-AI/SkyRL to the skyrl-project organisation.

name: rLLM
what_it_is: A framework for training language agents with RL where the same agent code drives evaluation and training: it runs CLI harnesses or your own agent, reads Harbor-compatible task folders, uses Docker, Daytona, Modal or local sandboxes, and switches between verl, Tinker and Fireworks backends with one flag.
use_it_when: You have an existing agent (or a CLI harness) and Harbor-style tasks, and want to move from evaluating it to training it without rewriting the agent.
source_note: GitHub README ('Core features'). The older agentica-project/rllm repo is stale (last push 2025-09-17); rllm-org/rllm is current.

name: ART (Agent Reinforcement Trainer)
what_it_is: An open-source RL framework that adds GRPO to an existing Python application: an OpenAI-compatible client records each rollout as a Trajectory, your code assigns its reward, and a server trains a LoRA and reloads it into vLLM; it also offers RULER, an LLM-judge reward.
use_it_when: Your agent already calls an OpenAI-style API and you want to train it on its own trajectories with few code changes, on a local GPU or a managed backend.
source_note: GitHub README ('ART Overview', 'Why ART?', 'Training Loop Overview', news on RULER).

name: Inspect
what_it_is: A framework for language-model evaluations with built-in components for prompts, tool use, multi-turn dialogue and model-graded scoring, plus over 200 ready-made evaluations.
use_it_when: You want to evaluate models (not train them) with careful logging and scoring, or reuse an existing safety or capability eval; OpenEnv can also run its environments through it.
source_note: GitHub README; OpenEnv README for the Inspect evaluation tutorial.

name: Terminal-Bench
what_it_is: A continuously updated benchmark of hard terminal tasks for agents, published as tagged releases on the Harbor Hub and run with `harbor run`; Terminal-Bench 2.1 is a separate repo that fixed tasks of 2.0, many for reward hacks.
use_it_when: You want real examples of well-built terminal tasks and verifiers, and of the ways graders get gamed, before writing your own.
source_note: GitHub README of harbor-framework/terminal-bench; harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 repo metadata. The original 1.0 repo is now harbor-framework/terminal-bench-1 (last push 2026-07-11).

name: SWE-Gym
what_it_is: An environment for training software-engineering agents and verifiers: 2.4K real Python tasks from 11 repos (plus a 234-task Lite split) with executable environments and test verification.
use_it_when: You want repository-level bug-fixing tasks to train or test a coding agent on; its README warns the environments contain a git shortcut to clean before use, or models can reward-hack.
source_note: GitHub README ('SWE-Gym Environment' section and the 'Patch before use' warning); paper 'Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym'.

name: AgentDojo
what_it_is: A dynamic environment for evaluating prompt-injection attacks and defences on tool-using agents, with task suites (such as workspace) and selectable attacks and defences.
use_it_when: You want to test whether an agent with tools can be hijacked by text hidden in tool results, and compare defences; its API is marked as still changing.
source_note: GitHub README (title, quickstart, benchmark script); paper 'AgentDojo' at arXiv 2406.13352.
